meta.title: The prisoners who mistook shadows for the world

plates.query: Rembrandt interior light from a window painting
plates.want: Rembrandt, blinding light at a doorway (PD)

plates.query: Raphael The School of Athens fresco

beats.text: Picture prisoners chained in a cave since birth, facing a blank wall.
Behind them a fire throws shadows on that wall. The shadows are the only world they have ever seen.
To them, the shadows are not pictures of things. The shadows are the things. They are reality.
Now drag one prisoner out into the sun. The light is agony. He begs to go back to the dark.
But slowly his eyes adjust, and he sees the real world the shadows were only copying.
Plato's question: if he returned to free the others, would they believe him — or kill him?
How much of what you call the world is just shadows you were raised to never doubt?

source_note: From The Republic, Book VII, trans. Benjamin Jowett (public domain).
